MFA No. 200589 of 2019  C/W MFA No. 202421 of 2017, MFA No.
 202422 of 2017, MFA No. 200587 of 2019  THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION. 173(1) OF MV ACT, PRAYING TO MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD PASSED IN MVC NO.441/2016 DATED-28.08.2017 BY THE IV ADDITIONAL DISTRICT JUDGE AND MEMBER, MACT NO.XIII, AT VIJAYAPURA AND ALLOW THIS APPEAL AND ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION AS CLAIMED IN THE CLAIM PETITION, IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.

THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, UMESH M. ADIGA J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Claimants in MVC No.441/2016 and MVC No.461/2016 have filed MFA No.200587/2019 and MFA No.200589/2019 respectively claiming for enhancement.

Respondent owner of the bus filed MFA No.202421/2017 and MFA No.202422/2017 respectively challenging the quantum and fastening entire liability on the respondent to pay compensation, in above cases, by the impugned judgment passed by the IV Addl. District Judge and MACT Vijayapura (hereafter after referred as 'the Tribunal' for short) dated 28.08.2017.

The Tribunal had clubbed MVC No.441/2016, 443/2016 and 461/2016 and passed the impugned common judgment and award dated 28.08.2017; same is challenged by both the claimant as well as owner of NC: 2023:KHC-K:1255-DB C/W MFA No.
202421 of 2017, MFA No. 202422 of 2017, MFA No. 200587 of 2019 the vehicle.
It appears no appeal is filed against award passed in MVC No.443/2016, by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: Though the matter is listed for hearing on admission; with the consent of both the sides, the matter is taken up for final disposal.

3. The case of claimants in both the petitions are that on 04.01.2016 deceased Anilkumar along with deceased Padmavati and Smt. Neelabai were going in motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-28-Q-2499,
towards Zalki;
They met with an accident near KEB Horti at about 2.30 p.m., due to rash and negligent driving of the bus bearing Reg.No.KA-25/F- 1800 by its driver.
Due to impact, Anilkmar and Smt. Padmavati sustained a grievous injuries and both succumbed to the injuries.
The claimant Smt. Neelabai had sustained injury.

Legal heirs of Anilkumar have filed MVC No.441/2015, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- and legal heirs of Smt. Padmavati have filed MVC No.461/2016,
claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-.
It is the contention of claimants in MVC No.441/2016 that deceased Anilkumar was aged about 34 years; he had irrigated agriculture lands of 8 acres.
He was growing grapes in the said lands and drying the same.
He was selling dried grapes.
He was also owning a Truck, flour mill and chilly grinding machine.
He was earning more than Rs.1,00,000/- per annum from the said source.
Claimants were depending upon his earnings.
The deceased was aged about 34 years.
With these reasons, they prayed to award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-.
5. Claimants in MVC No.461/2016, have contended that the deceased was their mother; she was an agriculturalist and earning Rs.30,000/- per month as a progressive farmer.

She dug 'Krishi Hond'
worth Rs.3,00,000/-.
She was contributing her earnings to the family.
Her age was 45 years.
With these reasons they prayed award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-.

6. Respondent has contended in both the claim petitions that accident was taken place due to rash and NC: 2023:KHC-K:1255-DB C/W MFA No. 202421 of 2017, MFA No. 202422 of 2017, MFA No.
200587 of 2019 negligent riding of motorcycle by its rider and driver of the bus was not at all responsible for the same.
Motorcycle was coming from opposite direction, by overtaking a Lorry in a rash and negligent manner.
The driver of the bus tried his level best to avoid the accident, till the rider of the motorcycle could not stop his vehicle and dashed against the front right side corner of the bus.
Thereafter, with an intention to claim compensation, fabricated the story stating that accident was taken place due to negligence of driver of the bus.
Therefore, prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
7. From the rival contention of the parties, the Tribunal had framed the necessary issues.
8. MVC No.441/2016, 443/2016 and 461/2016 were clubbed and common evidence was recorded.
Claimants examined PW1 to PW6 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P31.
Respondent examined RW1 and got marked Ex.R1 to Ex.R9.

partly allowed MVC No.441/2016 and MVC No.461/2016.

The Tribunal in MVC No.441/2016,
assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.10,000/- per month, his age as 37 years, deducted 1/4th of his income towards personal expenses and applied multiplier as 15 and awarded following compensation.

1. Loss of dependency - Rs.13,50,000/-
2. Loss of consortium - Rs.01,00,000/-
3. Love and affection - Rs.01,00,000/-

The Tribunal in MVC No.461/2016 assessed her age as 55 years.
The Tribunal held that the claimants are major son and daughters of deceased and were not depending upon her earnings.

The Tribunal has awarded global compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- under the following heads:
- 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1255-DB C/W MFA No. 202421 of 2017, MFA No. 202422 of 2017,
MFA No. 200587 of 2019 1) Loss of estate - Rs.75,000/-
2) Loss of love and affection - Rs.1,00,000/-
 3) Funeral and Transportation  expenses - Rs.25,000/-
The Tribunal held that accident was taken place due to contributory negligence of rider of the motorcycle i.e. husband of claimant No.2, who died in the accident and driver of bus.
The negligence of driver of bus and rider of motorcycle was apportioned in the ratio of 75%: 25% respectively.
The Tribunal directed respondent to pay 75% of the compensation in all three cases in the impugned judgment.
The same is challenged by the both the claimants as well as respondents in above said appeals.

sentences.text: We have heard the arguments.

The learned advocate for the claimants in MFA No.200587/2019 has contended that the Tribunal has not appreciated the evidence on record properly and erroneously assessed the income of deceased as Rs.10,000/-
per month.

Deceased was progressive farmer, he was owning agricultural - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1255-DB C/W MFA No. 202421 of 2017, MFA No. 202422 of 2017, MFA No.
200587 of 2019 implements and he was growing commercial crops like grapes and he used to dry them and sell the dried grapes.
He used to earn more profits.
In this regard, documents were placed by the appellant, but Tribunal did not consider them.
His further submissions are that the amount compensation awarded on other heads are also very meager, which needs to be reconsidered by this Court and prayed for enhancement.

13. The learned advocate for appellant in MFA No.200587/2019 has further submitted that accident was taken place due to rash and negligent driving of bus by its driver and not by the rider of the motorcycle.
However, Tribunal wrongly appreciated the evidence and held that deceased rider of the motorcycle had contributed to an extent of 25% to cause accident, which needs to be modified.
14. The learned advocate for the appellant in MFA No.202421/2017 has submitted that; accident was caused solely due to negligence of rider of motorcycle.

At the place of accident, the rider of the motorcycle was carrying two - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1255-DB C/W MFA No. 202421 of 2017, MFA No. 202422 of 2017, MFA No.
200587 of 2019 pillion riders against the permit condition.

Rider of motorcycle tried to overtake lorry, which was going a head of the motorcycle, without looking at the bus coming from the opposite direction; went to the wrong side of the road and dashed against front right portion of the bus.
These facts are mentioned in the charge sheet.

These acts of the rider of the motorcycle clearly indicates that he was solely responsible for causing of the accident and hence prayed to set aside impugned judgment fastening liability on respondent to pay the compensation.
15. The learned advocate for appellant in MFA No.202421/2017 has further contended that amount of compensation awarded are much on higher side without any basis.
Therefore, prayed to reconsider the same.

16. The learned advocate for appellant in MFA No.200589/2019 has submitted that the deceased was pillion rider, still the Tribunal held that to an extent of 25%, claimants are not entitled for compensation.

Even if the findings of Tribunal is accepted, then it was composite - 14 - Girimalla And Ors vs The Divisional Controller on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122486025/
8 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1255-DB C/W MFA No. 202421 of 2017, MFA No. 202422 of 2017, MFA No.
200587 of 2019 negligence of driver of the bus as well as rider of the motorcycle.

sentences.text: The owner and insurer of the motorcycle are not party in the present case and under circumstances, the claimants can claim compensation from the either of joint tortfeasor.
Therefore, the Tribunal ought to have directed respondent KSRTC to pay entire amount of compensation to the claimants.
He has further submitted that the amount of compensation awarded are on lesser side.
Therefore, prayed to enhance the compensation.
17. The following points emerges for determination.
1) Whether the accident was taken place due to contributory negligence of driver of the bus as well as rider of the motorcycle (deceased) and if so what is ratio of negligence?
2) Whether the compensation awarded to the claimants in MVC No.441/2016 and MVC No.461/2016 needs to be enhanced?
18. The fact of accident is not in dispute and death and injury to the rider of the motorcycle is also not in dispute.

Therefore, there is no need to reconsider the said - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1255-DB C/W MFA No. 202421 of 2017, MFA No. 202422 of 2017, MFA No.
200587 of 2019 fact.

The Tribunal in the impugned judgment at para No. 15 to 17 discussed the same and held that accident was taken place due to contributory negligence of driver of the bus as well as the rider of the motorcycle and apportioned the negligence in the ratio of 75: 25 of driver of the bus as well as the rider of the motorcycle respectively.
The said apportionment is seriously disputed by respondent-owner of bus on the ground that there was no negligence on the part of driver of the bus.
The learned advocate for both sides have taken us to the prosecution records.

The hand sketch map of spot of the accident prepared by the Investigating Officer shows that rider of the motorcycle while overtaking a lorry going a head on him, went to the right side of the road (wrong side of the road), might be without looking to the on coming bus from opposite side.
Similarly the driver of the bus could have taken it to left side of road margin or stopped the bus to avoid the collusion.
Looking into these circumstances, it indicates that negligence of the rider of the motorcycle as well as the driver of the bus are in equal proportion.

Though it is contended by the learned advocate - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1255-DB C/W MFA No. 202421 of 2017, MFA No. 202422 of 2017, MFA No.
200587 of 2019 for respondent that driver of the bus tried to avoid the accident, but looking to the scenario in Ex.P12, it is not probable.
Under these circumstances, the ratio of contribution of negligence of rider of the motorcycle as well as the driver of the bus is in the ratio of 50: 50 and not 75 :

sentences.text: 19. In MFA No.200587/2019 (MVC No.441/2016), the age of the deceased was determined by the Tribunal as 37 years on the basis of Ex.P4, it is undisputed.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.10,000/- per month.
The Tribunal in the impugned judgment at para No.18 has discussed in detail about the documents placed on record by the claimants in MVC No.441/2016.
Looking to the said documents, it appears he was a progressive farmer having irrigated lands.
Under these circumstances, assessing the income of deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month is on lower side.
Considering the evidence on record, income of the deceased per month is taken at RS.20,000/- from agriculture.
40% of his income has tobe added towards future prospects i.e. Rs.8,000/-.
Therefore his income was Rs.28,000/- per month.
Deceased left behind him four dependents.
Therefore, 1/4th on his earning shall be deducted towards personal expenses.
The net income on which the claimants were depending was Rs.21,000/-.
There is no dispute that the multiplier applicable to the facts of the case is 15.

Therefore, the amount of compensation under the head loss of dependency is Rs.21,000 x 12 x 15 = Rs.37,80,000/-.
21.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,00,000/- towards consortium and Rs.1,00,000/- towards love and affection.
It indicates that twice the compensation is awarded on the same head.

The Tribunal has not considered the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited V. Pranay Sethi and others1, and also in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and 2017 ACJ 2700 - 18 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1255-DB C/W MFA No. 202421 of 2017, MFA No. 202422 of 2017, MFA No.
200587 of 2019 others2.

22.
Claimants are entitled for following amount of compensation.

1. Loss of dependency - Rs.37,80,000/-
2. Loss of consortium - Rs.1,60,000/-

As held above, the deceased contributed to an extent of 50% for causing of the accident.

The claimants are not entitled to that extent of compensation from respondent- (2018)18 SCC 130 - 19 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1255-DB C/W MFA No. 202421 of 2017, MFA No. 202422 of 2017, MFA No.

The driver of the bus had contributed to an extent of 50% to cause the accident and hence respondent-KSRTC is liable to pay the 50% of the aforesaid compensation to the claimants i.e. Rs.19,85,000/- as against Rs.11,81,250/- awarded by Tribunal.
24. Claimants in MVC No.441/2016 are entitled for enhancement of Rs.8,03,750/-.
25. In MFA No.202422/2017 (MVC No.461/2016), the age of the deceased undisputedly is 55 years.
Tribunal has not awarded the compensation under the head loss of dependency on the ground that claimants are not dependent on income of the deceased.

It is not disputed that claimants are major sons of deceased; Eeven if they are not entitled for the compensation under the head loss of dependency, but they are entitled for compensation under the head loss of estate.
26. The Tribunal ought to have examined the fact and assessed the income of the deceased and also multiplier applicable to the case in hand.

The claimants have - 20 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1255-DB C/W MFA No. 202421 of 2017, MFA No. 202422 of 2017, MFA No.
200587 of 2019 contended that deceased was progressive agriculturist and they have produced Ex.P16 and Ex.P18 i.e. records of rights and bank ledger extract.
The said documents are not sufficient to hold that deceased was earning RS.30,000/- per month.
It is not stated regarding crops grown in the said land.
Claimants are sons of deceased appears to be residing with the deceased.
The age of the claimants No.1 to 3 are 38 years and 25 years respectively as on the date of claim petition (mentioned in cause title).
It appears they were managing the agricultural lands, even during the life time of deceased and continued it after her death also.
Therefore, notional income of the deceased has to be assessed.

27. Accident was taken place during the year 2016, while settlement of the dispute in Lok-Adalath in respect of MVC Cases, notional income of the victim of an accident held in the year 2016, is taken at Rs.8,750/-.
The same could be applied to the present case.
Deceased was aged about 55 years.
Therefore, 10% of income has to be added towards future prospects i.e. Rs.875/-.

The total income per month is Rs.9,625/-, the claimants are not dependents on Girimalla And Ors vs The Divisional Controller on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122486025/

30.

As rightly submitted by learned advocate for claimants, the Tribunal has erred in deducting 25%
of the compensation payable to the claimants on the ground that accident was taken place due to negligence of rider of the motorcycle to an extent of 25%.
It is pertinent to note that deceased was not rider of the motorcycle and she was a pillion rider.
She had not contributed for cause of the accident.

Respondent owner of the bus filed MFA No.202421/2017 and MFA No.202422/2017 respectively challenging the quantum and fastening entire liability on the respondent to pay compensation, in above cases, by the impugned judgment passed by the IV Addl. District Judge and MACT Vijayapura (hereafter after referred as 'the Tribunal' for short) dated 28.08.2017.
The Tribunal had clubbed MVC No.441/2016, 443/2016 and 461/2016 and passed the impugned common judgment and award dated 28.08.2017; same is challenged by both the claimant as well as owner of NC: 2023:KHC-K:1255-DB C/W MFA No.
202421 of 2017, MFA No. 202422 of 2017, MFA No. 200587 of 2019 the vehicle.
Due to impact, Anilkmar and Smt. Padmavati sustained a grievous injuries and both succumbed to the injuries.
The claimant Smt. Neelabai had sustained injury.
The Tribunal held that accident was taken place due to contributory negligence of rider of the motorcycle i.e. husband of claimant No.2, who died in the accident and driver of bus.
The negligence of driver of bus and rider of motorcycle was apportioned in the ratio of 75%: 25% respectively.
The Tribunal has not considered the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited V. 200587 of 2019 others2.
The Tribunal has not awarded compensation under the head loss of estate and more amount is awarded towards funeral expenses which needs to be recalculated and under the said conventional head of loss of estate and funeral expenses Rs.15,000/- each is awarded.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
These acts of the rider of the motorcycle clearly indicates that he was solely responsible for causing of the accident and hence prayed to set aside impugned judgment fastening liability on respondent to pay the compensation.
The owner and insurer of the motorcycle are not party in the present case and under circumstances, the claimants can claim compensation from the either of joint tortfeasor.
Therefore, the Tribunal ought to have directed respondent KSRTC to pay entire amount of compensation to the claimants.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Tribunal has not awarded the compensation under the head loss of dependency on the ground that claimants are not dependent on income of the deceased.
It is not disputed that claimants are major sons of deceased; Eeven if they are not entitled for the compensation under the head loss of dependency, but they are entitled for compensation under the head loss of estate.
26. The Tribunal ought to have examined the fact and assessed the income of the deceased and also multiplier applicable to the case in hand.
It appears they were managing the agricultural lands, even during the life time of deceased and continued it after her death also.
Therefore, notional income of the deceased has to be assessed.
Therefore, they are entitled for loss of consortium.
As held in the case of National Insurance Company Limited V. Pranay Sethi and others, and also in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others (supra), each shall be entitled for Rs.40,000/- under the said head and Rs.15,000/- shall be awarded towards funeral expenses.
It is pertinent to note that deceased was not rider of the motorcycle and she was a pillion rider.
She had not contributed for cause of the accident.
It is case of composite negligence of driver of the both the vehicles.
